author: For The Enterprise
title: Halifax County felon sentenced on federal fentanyl charge - NewsBreak
text:
By For The Enterprise ,
17 hours ago
A federal judge has sentenced Lorenizo Reshaud Simmons, 33, to more than six years in federal prison for possession with intent to sell over 40 grams of fentanyl, prosecutors announced Monday.
“Fentanyl kills kids,” U.S. Attorney Ellis Boyle said in a news release. “This repeat offender should have learned his lesson before, but he returned to this shameful exploitation of his own community. We should all join together in our close-knit eastern North Carolina communities to reject this evil and keep our families together. Simple lesson: drugs kill, prison awaits: Do right.”
Simmons sold fentanyl in Halifax County from a home he used to store and package his drugs, according to the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of North Carolina.
In August 2022, the Halifax County Sheriff’s Office launched an investigation into Simmons’ conduct after receiving complaints of drug activity in Garysburg. The sheriff’s office, with the assistance of the State Bureau of Investigation, conducted three controlled buys of fentanyl from Simmons.
On May 4, 2023, the HCSO and Northampton County Sheriff’s Office executed a search warrant at Simmons’ house, finding more than 300 grams of a fentanyl analogue, 90 milligrams of morphine, a digital scale, extended gun magazines, hundreds of bullets and other drug paraphernalia including needles and syringes.
Simmons is a convicted felon, most recently for selling opiates and possession of oxycodone in 2018.
Boyle, the district’s Senate-confirmed U.S. attorney, made the announcement after U.S. District Judge Louise W. Flanagan handed down the sentence in a New Bern courtroom. The HCSO, SBI and the Northampton County Sheriff’s Office investigated this case, and Assistant U.S. Attorney Kimberly Dixon prosecuted the case.
